title: Corner Sales Plan: First 10 Enterprise Customers
summary: The north star sales document for hitting $35k/month recurring from 10 paying Corner customers. Covers website, content, onboarding, outreach channels, sales process, retention, and 90-day execution timeline.
content:
Corner Sales Plan: First 10 Enterprise Customers at $3,500/month

Author: Steve (Sales Director) Date: 2026-03-22 Target: $35,000/month recurring revenue from 10 paying customers Timeline: 90 days from launch-ready product Status: ACTIVE -- this is the north star document

The Starting Position

Corner is not a concept. It is a working product with 240+ shipped features, 689 commits, four view modes, pixel art rooms, task management, agent chat, auth, settings, onboarding, a marketing page with pricing, battle cards, a case study, an ROI calculator, a 33-slide audit funnel, and 89 published skills. AOM runs its entire business on it every day. That is the proof.

What we don't have yet: a single paying customer. This plan fixes that.

What we sell

Corner gives small business owners an AI operations team that works 24/7 for less than one part-time employee.

Not software. Not a dashboard. A team. Agents that remember the business, talk to each other, hand off work, and get better every week. The owner opens their office in the morning, and the work is already done.

The number

10 customers x $3,500/month = $35,000/month = $420,000/year.

That number changes AOM. It funds a full-time employee, covers infrastructure, and proves the model. Everything in this plan is ruthlessly focused on hitting that number.

PHASE 1: The Website (aheadofmarket.com)

The current site has the pieces. /corner exists. /system exists. /book exists. /roi-calculator exists. /audit/test exists. What's missing is a single, unified sales flow that takes a visitor from "what is this?" to "take my money" in under 3 minutes.

1.1 The Corner Landing Page (Rebuild /corner)

The current /corner page has pricing tiers (Audit $2.5k, Starter $1.5k/mo, Growth $2.5k/mo, Enterprise $10k+). The tiers are right. The page is wrong. It reads like a feature list. It needs to read like a job posting for the team the prospect always wanted but could never afford.

New page structure (top to bottom):

Hero

  • Headline: "Your AI team is ready."
  • Subhead: "Corner gives your business a team of AI agents that handles scheduling, follow-up, outreach, content, and quality control. 24/7. For less than one employee."
  • Primary CTA: "See it in action" (scrolls to interactive demo section)
  • Secondary CTA: "Book a demo" (links to /book)
  • Background: the voxel office PNG (day version). This is the differentiator. No other product looks like this. Lead with it.

The Problem (3 cards)

  • Card 1: "You're the bottleneck." 15-20 hours/week on admin. Leads fall through cracks. Client follow-up is inconsistent. You do everything because nobody else can.
  • Card 2: "Tools don't fix it." You've tried Zapier, ChatGPT, project management apps. They add more screens to check, not fewer hours to work.
  • Card 3: "Hiring is expensive." A part-time office manager costs $30-40k/year. A marketing person costs $50k+. And they still need managing.

The Solution (full-width section with game screenshot)

  • Corner is not another tool. It's a team. You get agents that specialize: one handles your schedule, one manages client follow-up, one does your outreach, one creates content, one checks everyone's work.
  • Show the isometric office screenshot. Label the rooms. Make it feel alive.
  • Key line: "They remember your business. They talk to each other. They work while you sleep."

How It Works (3 steps)

  1. We audit your business (free 30-min call). We map your operations, find the bottlenecks, identify where AI agents save you the most time.
  2. We build your team. In 48 hours, your Corner office is live with agents trained on your business. Your projects, your clients, your workflows.
  3. You run your business. Open Corner in the morning. Your agents have already handled follow-ups, drafted responses, organized tasks, and flagged anything that needs you. Review, approve, move on.

Pricing (simplified from 4 tiers to 3)

The current 4-tier model is too complex for the target buyer. Simplify:

Plan Price What You Get
Starter $1,500/month 3 agents, 1 project, basic task management, email support
Growth $3,500/month 6 agents, unlimited projects, full task + chat, priority support, weekly check-in call
Enterprise $8,000+/month Unlimited agents, dedicated infrastructure, custom integrations, on-site setup, Slack/Teams connect

Growth is the target tier. $3,500/month. That's the number. Badge it "Most Popular." Every CTA on the page pushes toward Growth.

Drop the one-time Audit tier from the pricing page. The audit is the sales tool, not a product. Offer it free as part of the sales process. It qualifies the prospect AND gives them a taste. Charging $2,500 for an audit before they've seen the product creates friction at the worst possible moment.

Social Proof

  • "AOM runs its entire business on Corner." Full case study link.
  • Stats: 689 commits shipped. 13 agents. 240+ features. 89 skills.
  • Ambition Mechanical testimonial (when available).
  • Target: 3 logos + 3 testimonial quotes within 60 days of first customer.

FAQ (6 questions)

  1. "What happens if an agent makes a mistake?" Every agent's work goes through a QA agent before you see it. Nothing ships without review.
  2. "Can I talk to my agents?" Yes. Same as messaging a coworker. Type a message, get a response. They remember everything.
  3. "What if I want to change something?" Your account manager (that's us) adjusts agents, adds skills, and reconfigures workflows. Included in your plan.
  4. "How is this different from ChatGPT?" ChatGPT answers one question at a time. Corner runs six agents in parallel, connected to your actual business data, 24/7. (Pull from battle card #1.)
  5. "What happens if I cancel?" Your data is yours. We export everything. No lock-in. Month-to-month.
  6. "Is my business data safe?" SOC 2 compliance roadmap. Isolated infrastructure per client. No shared data. (This becomes real with C4 Docker-per-client.)

Final CTA

  • "Ready to meet your team? Book a 30-minute demo."
  • Calendar booking widget (Calendly or Cal.com) embedded directly. No extra clicks.

1.2 The Demo Page (Rebuild /demo)

The current demo page has an 8-9 step scripted walkthrough. That's good bones. But it needs to convert, not just impress.

Changes:

  • After the walkthrough completes, show a CTA overlay: "That was 60 seconds. Imagine 60 days. Book your demo."
  • Add a "Build Your Office" mini-experience: visitor enters their business name, picks 3 agents from a role list (Scheduler, Follow-Up, Outreach, Content, QA, Estimating), and sees a custom office preview generate in real-time. This is the hook. They see their name on the building. Their agents in the rooms. Then: "Want this for real? Book a call."
  • The demo page URL becomes the primary link in all outreach emails, LinkedIn posts, and social content.

1.3 Pages to Build

Page Purpose Owner Priority
/corner (rebuild) Primary sales page Bobby + Steffen P0
/demo (rebuild) Interactive conversion tool Bobby P0
/pricing Standalone pricing page (linked from /corner, also standalone URL for email/link sharing) Bobby + Steffen P0
/terms Terms of Service Legal template + Bobby P1 (blocks Stripe)
/privacy Privacy Policy Legal template + Bobby P1 (blocks Stripe)
/case-study (update) AOM's own Corner story with real metrics Bobby + Steve P1
/one-pager Web version of the sales one-pager (already specced) Bobby + Steffen P2

PHASE 2: Content + Demos

The game is the product's unfair advantage. Nothing else in the market looks like Corner. Cleo and Tony need to weaponize that visual identity.

2.1 Core Demo Video (Cleo)

"Meet Your Team" -- 90 seconds

This is the hero video. It lives on /corner, gets shared on LinkedIn, runs as the first thing in a sales call screen-share.

Script outline:

  • 0-10s: Black screen. Text: "You're drowning in admin." Beat. "What if you weren't?"
  • 10-25s: Corner office fades in. Camera slowly pans across the isometric world. Rooms are lit up. Agents are working. The vibe is alive.
  • 25-40s: Zoom into one room. Show a task flowing in. Agent picks it up. Message appears in chat. Task moves to completed. 15 seconds of real workflow.
  • 40-55s: Pull back to the full office. Show multiple rooms active simultaneously. Overlay text: "6 agents. Working in parallel. 24/7."
  • 55-70s: Show the checklist view. Real tasks getting checked off. Overlay: "You check in for 10 minutes in the morning."
  • 70-85s: Show the notification toast. "Agent completed: Client follow-up for Johnson Electric." Overlay: "They work. You approve."
  • 85-90s: Corner logo. "Your AI team is ready. aheadofmarket.com/corner"

Production notes for Cleo:

  • Screen record the actual product. Not mockups. Real dashboard, real data, real agent chat.
  • Use the day mode office (warm, inviting). Night mode for a "they work while you sleep" B-roll clip.
  • Music: ambient, confident, minimal. Think Apple product video. Not corporate. Not hype.
  • Export: 16:9 for YouTube/website, 9:16 vertical crop for Instagram/TikTok, 1:1 square crop for LinkedIn feed.

2.2 Short Social Clips (Cleo + Tony)

6 clips, 15-30 seconds each. One per week for 6 weeks.

# Clip Hook Visual
1 "The Morning Check-In" "This is what my morning looks like now." Open Corner, scroll through completed tasks, approve 3 things, close laptop. Done in 2 minutes.
2 "The Agent Handoff" "Watch this agent hand work to another agent." Screen record of a task moving from one room to another. Celebration animation.
3 "The Night Shift" "My AI team works while I sleep." Time-lapse: night mode office, agents moving between rooms, tasks completing, notifications stacking up. Morning: owner opens dashboard, everything's done.
4 "The Room Tour" "Let me show you my office." Pan through each room. Quick label: "This is my scheduler. This is my content creator. This is my QA."
5 "Before and After" "Monday before Corner vs. Monday after." Split screen: left side is chaos (emails, missed calls, sticky notes). Right side is Corner dashboard, clean, organized, tasks flowing.
6 "The Demo" "Build your AI office in 60 seconds." Speed-run the onboarding: name business, pick agents, office appears. CTA: "Try it."

Posting schedule (Tony):

  • LinkedIn: 2x/week (Tue + Thu). Longer format clips (#1, #3, #5).
  • Instagram Reels: 2x/week (Mon + Wed). Shorter clips (#2, #4, #6).
  • TikTok: Mirror Instagram. Same clips, platform-native captions.
  • Twitter/X: 1x/week (Fri). Screenshot + one-liner + link to demo.

2.3 Interactive Demo Experience

The /demo page rebuild (Phase 1.2) IS the interactive experience. But we also need a self-service version that requires zero human interaction.

Self-service demo flow:

  1. Visitor lands on /demo
  2. Watches the scripted walkthrough (existing 8-step)
  3. Gets prompted: "Want to try it with YOUR business?"
  4. Enters: business name, industry (dropdown: Construction, CPA, Agency, Restaurant, Other), biggest pain point (dropdown: scheduling, follow-up, admin, content, all of the above)
  5. Corner generates a preview office: their business name on the building, 3-4 agents pre-selected based on industry + pain point, sample tasks pre-populated
  6. They can click rooms, see agent bios, see sample completed tasks
  7. Final screen: "This is what 30 days looks like. [Show mock metrics: 47 tasks completed, 12 follow-ups sent, 8 hours saved/week]. Ready? [Book a Call] [Start Free Trial]"

This is the conversion machine. The prospect builds emotional ownership before they ever talk to a human.

PHASE 3: Signup to First Login

The gap between "I'm interested" and "I'm inside the product" is where most SaaS products lose people. Corner's onboarding must be zero-friction and instantly valuable.

3.1 Auth (Partially Built)

Current state: Supabase auth exists. Email/password login. Session persistence. AuthGuard redirects to /onboarding. Client ID reads from user metadata.

What needs to happen:

  • Lock down the sessionStorage.setItem('dash-auth','1') bypass before any real client touches it. One line removal.
  • Ensure /onboarding and /elon-room are in vercel.json (they're currently missing -- direct URL access returns 404).
  • Add Google OAuth as a signup option. Business owners don't want to create another password. "Sign in with Google" reduces signup friction by 30-40% (industry benchmark).
  • Add the force-password-change flow for admin-provisioned accounts (isTempPassword is already built).

3.2 The Intro Story (Conversational Onboarding)

Current onboarding: 5-step wizard (Welcome > Name workspace > Place first room > Done). That's functional. But it's not magic.

New onboarding flow (replaces current wizard):

Screen 1: "What's your business called?"

  • Single text input. Big. Centered. The workspace name.
  • As they type, the isometric office fades in behind the input field with their name on the building.
  • "Continue" button.

Screen 2: "What do you do?"

  • Industry selector: Construction, CPA/Accounting, Agency/Consulting, Restaurant/Hospitality, Real Estate, Other
  • Sub-selector for Construction: HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, General Contractor, Roofing, Other
  • This data drives which agents and skills get pre-loaded.

Screen 3: "What's eating your time?"

  • Multi-select (pick up to 3): Scheduling, Client follow-up, Estimating, Invoicing, Content/Social Media, Lead generation, Employee management, Bookkeeping
  • These map directly to agent roles. Selected pains = pre-configured agents.

Screen 4: "Meet your team."

  • The office is now populated. 3-6 agents based on their selections.
  • Each agent has a name, a role, and a one-line intro: "I'm Bobby. I handle your website and online presence."
  • Short typewriter animation for each agent introducing themselves. 2-3 seconds per agent. Total: 10-15 seconds.
  • The emotional peak: the prospect sees a team that was built FOR them, based on what they just said.

Screen 5: "Let's get to work."

  • The office is live. Sample tasks are pre-populated based on industry:
    • Construction: "Follow up with Johnson Electric re: Tuesday estimate" / "Post this week's project photos to Instagram" / "Send invoice reminder to pending clients"
    • CPA: "Send tax deadline reminder to Q1 clients" / "Draft response to IRS notice for Smith account" / "Schedule next week's client meetings"
  • One task is already "in progress" with an agent working on it. The prospect can watch it complete.
  • First real interaction: "Type a message to any agent." Chat input is focused. They type something. The agent responds.
  • They're in.

3.3 Auto-Build Logic

The onboarding selections drive automatic configuration:

Industry Default Agents Default Skills
Construction (HVAC/Plumbing/Electrical) Scheduler, Follow-Up, Estimating Support, Content Creator, QA Calendar sync, invoice drafts, project photo posting, client reminder emails
CPA/Accounting Scheduler, Client Manager, Document Prep, Outreach, QA Tax deadline tracking, client document requests, IRS notice drafting, meeting scheduling
Agency/Consulting Project Manager, Content Creator, Outreach, Client Tracker, QA Proposal drafting, social media scheduling, project status updates, invoice tracking
Restaurant/Hospitality Scheduler, Social Media, Review Manager, Inventory, QA Shift scheduling, Instagram posting, Google review responses, supplier ordering
Real Estate Lead Manager, Follow-Up, Content Creator, Scheduler, QA Lead nurturing sequences, listing descriptions, open house scheduling, market updates

This is not cosmetic. When a construction company owner signs up and sees agents named after construction workflows with construction-specific sample tasks, they immediately believe this was built for them. That belief is worth more than any feature.

3.4 First 5 Minutes

After onboarding completes, the prospect is in their office. The critical first 5 minutes:

  • Minute 0-1: They see the office. It's populated. Agents are working. One task is completing right now.
  • Minute 1-2: A notification toast appears: "Agent completed: [industry-specific task]." They see the completed task in the feed.
  • Minute 2-3: They get a message from their router agent (Elon-equivalent): "Welcome to Corner. I'm your operations coordinator. I've set up your team based on what you told us. Here's what's happening right now: [bulleted list of active tasks]. What would you like me to focus on first?"
  • Minute 3-5: They respond. The agent responds. They're having a conversation with their AI team. They're hooked.

If they close the browser and come back the next day, the agents should have "completed" demo tasks overnight. The prospect opens Corner to a list of completed work. That's the moment they think: "I need this."

PHASE 4: First 10 Customers

4.1 Who Are They?

The first 10 are not random people who find Corner on Google. The first 10 are hand-picked by Patrik and Ash based on these criteria:

Tier 1 (Customers 1-3): Warm Network

  • Business owners Patrik or Ash know personally
  • Already trust AOM (past clients, friends, referrals)
  • Industry: construction or professional services
  • Can absorb $3,500/month without board approval
  • Willing to be a case study and provide a testimonial
  • Phoenix metro (can do in-person demos)

Tier 2 (Customers 4-7): Warm Referrals

  • Referred by Tier 1 customers
  • Ambition Mechanical's network (HVAC/plumbing/electrical contacts)
  • Chamber of Commerce contacts
  • AOM's existing prospect pipeline (PA-LA, Intelliplay, Sure Leverage)
  • LinkedIn connections of Patrik's who are business owners

Tier 3 (Customers 8-10): Targeted Outreach

  • From Jacob's AZ ROC database (45k+ licensed contractors)
  • CPA firms found through public directories
  • Selected based on: 5-25 employees, Phoenix metro, active social presence (indicates they care about growth), no obvious IT department
  • Outreach via personal email from Patrik, not mass blast

4.2 Where Do We Find Them?

Channel 1: Personal outreach by Patrik and Ash (Tier 1)

Patrik and Ash each make a list of 15 business owners they know. That's 30 names. Of those 30, 5-10 will take a meeting. Of those meetings, 3 will convert. This is the highest-conversion channel because trust is pre-built.

Play: Personal text message. Not email. Not LinkedIn DM. Text.

"Hey [name], we built something I want to show you. We've been running our entire business on it and it's working. It's an AI team that handles the back-office stuff -- scheduling, follow-up, content, task management. I think it could save you 10-15 hours a week. Can I show you in 15 minutes? Coffee's on me."

That message gets opened. That message gets a response. The meeting happens at their office or over coffee. Patrik demos on his actual Corner instance. Not slides. Not a fake demo. The real thing.

Channel 2: LinkedIn (Tier 2)

Patrik's LinkedIn profile becomes a Corner case study. Every post for the next 90 days tells the story of running a business with AI agents.

Post types:

  • "My AI team completed 47 tasks while I was at my kid's baseball game" (screenshot of completed tasks)
  • "Here's what my office looks like at 6am" (screenshot of night mode, agents working)
  • "This agent saved me 3 hours yesterday on client follow-up" (specific example)
  • "I built an AI team for my construction client. Here's what happened in 30 days." (Ambition case study)

Each post ends with: "DM me 'CORNER' if you want to see it."

DMs get the demo link. Demo link leads to a booking. Booking leads to a sale.

Channel 3: Industry Events + Local Networking (Tier 2-3)

Phoenix has active business communities:

  • Phoenix Chamber of Commerce
  • Local HVAC/contractor trade associations
  • Arizona CPA Society events
  • Small business meetups (SCORE, SBA workshops)
  • AI-focused meetups (growing fast in Phoenix)

Patrik attends with a simple pitch: "I run a creative studio. We built AI agents that run our back office. Now we're offering it to other businesses." Hand them the one-pager (already specced by Steve). QR code goes to /demo.

Target: 2 events per month. 5 meaningful conversations per event. 1 meeting booked per event. Over 90 days, that's 6 meetings and 2-3 conversions.

Channel 4: Cold Email (Tier 3)

Jacob already has 51+ emails sent and 33 drafts pending. The cold email channel is built. The message needs to change.

Old approach: zero-risk offers, spotlight series, free content production. All dead.

New approach: outcome-based. Short. Specific.

Email template:

Subject: Quick question about [their business name]

[First name],

I run a creative and AI studio in Phoenix. We built an operations system that gives small businesses an AI team handling scheduling, follow-up, outreach, and admin.

Our HVAC client went from 15 hours/week on admin to 3. Our agency went from missing 30% of follow-ups to zero.

I'd love to show you how it works for [their industry]. 15 minutes, no pitch. Just a demo.

[Calendar link]

Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com/corner

Volume: 10 targeted emails per week. Not mass blast. Each email references the prospect's actual business name and industry. Jacob segments, Patrik personalizes the top 3 per week.

4.3 The Sales Process

Every prospect goes through the same 4-step process:

Step 1: Discovery Call (15 minutes)

  • Ask 5 questions:
    1. What does your week look like? Walk me through Monday.
    2. What's the thing that makes you say "I wish someone else handled this"?
    3. How many hours a week do you spend on admin/back-office?
    4. Have you tried any AI tools? What happened?
    5. If I could give you back 10 hours a week, what would you do with them?
  • Don't sell. Listen. Take notes. This call is a qualification.
  • End with: "I want to show you something. Can we do 30 minutes next week?"

Step 2: Live Demo (30 minutes)

  • Screen share Patrik's actual Corner instance. Real agents. Real tasks. Real data.
  • Show the morning check-in: open Corner, see what agents did overnight, approve 3 things.
  • Show a task creation: type a message to an agent, watch it respond, see the task appear in the board.
  • Show the game view. Let them react to the isometric office. Nobody expects this. It's the moment.
  • Last 5 minutes: "Here's what this would look like for your business." Pull up the custom demo (from Phase 2.3) with their business name and industry-specific agents.
  • End with: "We're taking 10 businesses for our first cohort. $3,500/month. We build everything. You approve. Want in?"

Step 3: Proposal (24 hours after demo)

  • Send the one-pager (PDF) with a custom cover: their business name, their selected agents, estimated hours saved per week.
  • Include a simple contract: month-to-month, $3,500/month, 48-hour setup, 30-day money-back guarantee.
  • Link to /terms and /privacy.
  • Stripe payment link for first month.

Step 4: Close (within 7 days)

  • One follow-up text at Day 3 if no response: "Hey [name], just checking -- did you have any questions about Corner?"
  • One follow-up email at Day 5 with a testimonial or case study update.
  • Day 7: move to nurture if no close. Add to monthly newsletter list.

4.4 The Pitch (Not Features, Outcomes)

Never say: "Corner has 240 features, 4 view modes, and a hex grid."

Always say:

For Construction: "You spend 15 hours a week on scheduling, estimates, and follow-ups. Corner does it in 15 minutes. Your crew is on the job. Your clients get responses same-day. Your estimates go out before the competition's. And you're home for dinner."

For CPA: "Tax season is 14-hour days. Corner handles the client reminders, the document requests, the scheduling, and the follow-up emails. You focus on the returns. Your agents handle everything around the returns."

For Agencies: "You lose 30% of prospects because follow-up falls through the cracks. Corner's follow-up agent never forgets. Every lead gets a response. Every client gets an update. Every project stays on track. While you do the creative work."

4.5 What Makes Them Stay After Month 1

This is the retention question. The answer is simple: the system gets smarter.

Week 1: Corner runs on demo data + initial configuration. The prospect is learning the product. They're messaging agents, assigning tasks, exploring views.

Week 2-3: The agents have learned the business context. Responses are specific to their clients, their projects, their patterns. The prospect starts trusting the agents to draft real emails and schedule real meetings.

Week 4: The first monthly review. AOM presents: tasks completed (count), estimated hours saved (calculated from task volume x average manual time), active projects (count), agent utilization (% of time working vs. idle). This is the ROI proof. If the numbers say "Corner saved you 40 hours this month," that's $3,500 for 40 hours of work. That's $87.50/hour. Cheaper than any employee.

Month 2+: The prospect can't imagine going back. Their operations depend on Corner. They've stopped doing the admin work themselves. The switching cost is now psychological: "I'd have to do all this manually again."

That's the retention engine. Not features. Dependency.

PHASE 5: Retention + Expansion

5.1 Monthly Check-ins

Every Growth customer gets a 30-minute monthly review call with Patrik or Ash.

Agenda:

  1. Review the numbers: tasks completed, hours saved, agent performance
  2. What's working? What's frustrating?
  3. New features shipped this month (Corner releases weekly)
  4. Adjust agent configuration based on feedback
  5. Ask: "Who else in your network should see this?"

The monthly call is non-negotiable for the first 10 customers. These are the founding customers. Their feedback shapes the product. Their satisfaction generates referrals.

5.2 Upsell Path ($3,500 to $5,000+)

The upsell is natural, not forced.

Month 2-3: Offer to add agents. "Your follow-up agent is handling 30 interactions/week. Want a dedicated estimating agent? That's one more agent on your Growth plan."

Month 3-4: Introduce premium skills. "We built a new skill that auto-generates project proposals from your estimate data. Want to try it for a month?"

Month 6: Move to Enterprise. "You're running 8 agents now and processing 200+ tasks/month. You've outgrown Growth. Enterprise gives you unlimited agents, dedicated infrastructure, and direct Slack integration. $8,000/month."

The path: $3,500 (Growth) -> $5,000 (Growth + add-on agents/skills) -> $8,000 (Enterprise).

Each upsell is triggered by usage data, not a calendar. When the system shows the customer is bumping against plan limits, that's the conversation.

5.3 Case Studies from First 10

Every founding customer becomes a case study. Non-negotiable as part of the founding cohort agreement.

Case study structure:

  • Before Corner: hours/week on admin, pain points, missed opportunities
  • After Corner: hours saved, tasks automated, specific wins
  • Quote from the owner
  • Screenshot of their Corner office (with permission)
  • Published at /case-study/[business-name]

Timeline:

  • Month 1: AOM's own case study (already exists, update with metrics)
  • Month 2: First customer case study (30 days of data)
  • Month 3: Second and third customer case studies
  • By month 6: 5+ case studies covering construction, CPA, and at least one other industry

Case studies are the sales flywheel. Each case study makes the next sale easier. By customer #10, the sales call includes: "Here are 5 businesses like yours already running on Corner. Here's what happened."

5.4 Referral Program

After month 2, introduce a referral incentive.

Offer: Refer a business that signs up, get $500 off your next month. No limit.

A customer paying $3,500/month who refers 3 friends pays $2,000 that month. They're incentivized to evangelize. The referred prospect comes in pre-sold by someone they trust. Conversion rate on referrals: 30-50% (vs. 2-5% on cold outreach).

Target: each of the first 10 customers refers 1-2 businesses within 6 months. That's 10-20 warm leads from people already using and loving the product.

EXECUTION TIMELINE

Weeks 1-2: Foundation

  • Bobby rebuilds /corner landing page (new structure from Phase 1.1)
  • Bobby builds /pricing as standalone page
  • Bobby builds /terms and /privacy (from legal templates)
  • Bobby fixes /onboarding and /elon-room vercel.json routes
  • Bobby removes sessionStorage auth bypass
  • Bobby replaces hardcoded DEFAULT_PROJECTS with Supabase-driven per-client pills
  • Steffen designs the new /corner page (hero, pricing cards, social proof)
  • Steve writes final copy for /corner and /pricing
  • Cleo begins production on "Meet Your Team" 90-second video

Weeks 3-4: Content + Demo

  • Cleo delivers "Meet Your Team" video (3 crops: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1)
  • Cleo produces first 3 social clips (#1 Morning Check-In, #2 Agent Handoff, #3 Night Shift)
  • Bobby rebuilds /demo with custom office builder
  • Bobby adds Google OAuth to signup
  • Bobby builds the auto-configuration onboarding (industry -> agents -> tasks)
  • Tony begins posting schedule (LinkedIn 2x/week, IG 2x/week)

Weeks 5-6: Sales Engine

  • Patrik + Ash make their 30-name warm list
  • Patrik sends first 10 personal texts
  • First 3 discovery calls booked
  • Jacob shifts cold email template to outcome-based approach
  • Jacob sends 10 targeted emails/week
  • Patrik attends first industry event with one-pager
  • Case study page updated with real metrics

Weeks 7-8: First Closes

  • First live demo conducted
  • First proposal sent (one-pager + contract + Stripe link)
  • Customer #1 signed
  • Customer #1 onboarded within 48 hours
  • Cleo produces clips #4-6
  • Second round of discovery calls

Weeks 9-12: Scale to 10

  • Customers 2-5 signed (warm network + referrals)
  • First customer case study published (30 days of data)
  • Customers 6-8 from LinkedIn + events
  • Customers 9-10 from cold outreach + referrals
  • Monthly review process established
  • Referral program launched
  • $35,000/month MRR achieved

DEPENDENCIES (Engineering Must-Haves)

These are not my problems to solve. These are Bobby's tickets. But they block sales if they're not done.

Blocker Why It Blocks Sales Owner Timeline
